## Recording the version-of-record

Where the version-of-record lives, how it's stored and surfaced, and how often it changes. Pick the
case that fits your medium:

- **Manifest**, where the version-of-record is stored:
  - if Rust, `Cargo.toml` `[package].version`
  - if Python, `pyproject.toml` `[project].version` (or the committed config it's sourced from)
  - otherwise wherever the medium records it (a generic `version.toml`, a book's frontmatter, ...).
    Add the case as needed
- **Notation**, how the `-` form is stored. See [Grammar and storage](#grammar-and-storage):
  - if the format allows `-` (TOML `version.toml`, `Cargo.toml`), store it verbatim
  - if it bars `-` (PEP 440's local segment, e.g. a Python project), remap to `+`, so `0.3.0-5.3.0`
    becomes `0.3.0+5.3.0`: same version, just the stored spelling
- **Reporter**, how a built artifact surfaces the version-of-record:
  - if a CLI app, `<cli-app> -V`
  - if a TUI/GUI, add to Help/About or display on the title
- **Cadence**, how often to bump: see [Unique per
  commit](#unique-per-commit-preference-not-requirement). This project follows the per-commit
  preference.

## Dev artifact name

When other projects consume the built artifact (e.g. the installed CLI) while this repo is under
active development, the dev build installs under a separate name so a mid-cycle install never
clobbers the binary consumers are running:

- **Name**: the manifest's package name carries a `-dev` suffix (`<name>` -> `<name>-dev`). If Rust,
  `[package].name`, so the per-commit flow's `cargo install` produces `<name>-dev` and leaves plain
  `<name>` untouched.
- **Constant, not per-step**: the step already lives in the version-of-record (`<name>-dev -V`
  reports the exact rung). A per-step name would churn the manifest every commit and litter the
  install dir with stale binaries.
- **Promotion**: plain `<name>` updates only by an explicit act: a separate clone built at the
  chosen commit with the plain name (or a copy of the dev binary), never by the per-commit flow's
  install.

**Single-name variant**: a repo striving to release makes the package name the binary's name, plain
`<name>` on `main` only:

- **The opening renames**: its bump sets `<name>-dev` beside the suffixed version, and every rung
  and the closing build under the dev name, the closing over the bare version.
- **Land restores**: the rename back to `<name>` is Land's act, so the stable name is only ever
  installed from what `main` will carry.
- **A build script guards the pairing** on every cargo verb: a suffixed version under the stable
  name fails the build, so no mid-cycle install can clobber the consumers' binary.

## Unique per commit (preference, not requirement)

Our general notion is that the version-of-record should change on **every commit**, so a built or
running artifact identifies the exact commit it came from.

- This is a preference, **not** a hard requirement. A project following the cycle protocol may bump
  less often: once per cycle, only at release, and so on. Record the choice in [Recording the
  version-of-record](#recording-the-version-of-record) if it differs.
- It is achievable because the cycle's versions (below) are **pre-assignable**, unlike the git SHA,
  which a commit cannot contain.

## Suffix scheme

The cycle (opening -> commits -> closing, per the [Cycle protocol](../AGENTS.md#cycle-protocol))
encodes each commit's phase in the version suffix, the **final identifier `0` marking a
Preparation**.

This is the manifest's own spelling, read by whoever inspects `Cargo.toml` or `-V` output. It is not
a name for a step: a step is identified by its title, and an in-flight ladder rung carries neither a
number nor a version (see [Steps are named, not numbered](prose.md#steps-are-named-not-numbered)).
The identifiers below count commits within a phase, and nothing dereferences one.

- `X.Y.Z-0`: Preparation
- `X.Y.Z-1`, `X.Y.Z-2`, ...: the commits between
- `X.Y.Z`: Close-out (bare version, no suffix)

**Preparation is optional.** A lightweight cycle, with no ladder and no setup commit, skips `-0` and
starts at `-1` (its first commit). A single-step cycle is one commit, the Close-out, and carries the
bare `X.Y.Z` ([Cycle shape](../AGENTS.md#cycle-shape)). The same holds at every level: a sub-cycle
needing no Preparation omits its `.0` (see Nesting). One that grows a Preparation later adds the `0`
step without renumbering siblings.

Disambiguation:

- `-10`: commit #10 (final identifier `10`), not a Preparation.
- `-1.0`: Preparation of the `-1` sub-cycle (final identifier `0`).

**Nesting.** Sub-cycles append another level, recursively:

- `X.Y.Z-3.0`: Preparation of the `-3` sub-cycle
- `X.Y.Z-3.1`, `X.Y.Z-3.2`: its commits between
- `X.Y.Z-3`: its Close-out
- `X.Y.Z-3.1.0`: Preparation of the `-3.1` sub-sub-cycle

Bump the version-of-record at the start of every step (the per-commit checklist carries the step),
so the manifest always records the commit it will be part of and, per the preference above, every
commit carries a distinct version.

## Agent-files version

# Closed: the last cycle's record

The last finished cycle's record, whole. A cycle's closing replaces this file's `## Closed` with
its own block from [zDOING.md](zDOING.md) and this file's references with that block's, so the
last record stays here until the next one is finished. Earlier cycles are in each landmark
commit's copy of the record.

## Closed

### chore: the sandbox's names leave .gitignore

(wink + agent, 2026-10-12, picked 2026-10-14) Claude Code's sandbox puts empty files at a
workspace's root while an agent's command runs, `.bashrc`, `.gitconfig`, `.mcp.json`,
`.claude/settings.json`, and some twenty more. A snapshot taken from outside that sandbox at that
moment sees them as new files, and a push commits them: 23 went into a commit in the two-session
tests ([session-lock.md](notes/session-lock.md)). The Todo entry picked is "init writes the agent
sandbox's names into .gitignore":

- This repo's `.gitignore` names them, added by hand, and the one `init` writes has four lines
  and none of them.
- `init` writes the names, and a workspace made before it does gets them by hand or by a command
  that brings a workspace up to date.
- The list is Claude Code's and can change with a release, so where it is kept, and how it is
  checked against what the sandbox does, is settled in the cycle.
- We think a user's own `jj st` beside a running agent command sees the files too. Not tested.

#### Deliberation

- The names are ignored nowhere, wink's lean and the cycle's finding: an ordinary command leaves
  nothing jj records.
  - Inside the sandbox a protected name that does not exist is `/dev/null` mounted for the life of
    the command, a character device, and jj snapshots no device. A `jj st` run there with the
    names unignored listed only the cycle's edits.
  - Tested with wink watching Zed: a sandboxed command held for 20 seconds showed the eleven root
    names for exactly that long, and the same command unsandboxed showed none.
  - Seen in the sandbox's own arguments: `bwrap` mounts `/dev/null` over each missing protected
    path by name, before it starts the shell.
  - What the ignore hid in this repo were real files: 24 left on disk at 2026-10-11T21:09:22Z by
    the session lock's holder, a background command ended with its session, so the cleanup an
    ordinary command gets did not run. wink deleted them, 2026-10-14.
  - The cost accepted: a snapshot or commit made outside the sandbox while an agent command runs
    sees the files. wink's editor listed them for some seconds, twice, during the cycle's edits.
  - The cost avoided, wink's reason: an ignored name hides a file a user makes there. It is never
    committed, and nothing says so until a clone comes up without it. The flicker is surprising
    and visible, the loss is silent.
  - Weighed and not taken: `init` writing the list, and the list in each user's global git ignore.
    The list is Claude Code's, changes with a release, and names files a project may track.
- The direction was reversed twice before it settled. A probe with the leftovers still on disk
  showed all eleven root names in an in-sandbox `jj st`, which argued for the ignore. The
  leftovers' birth times then showed they were not the sandbox's per-command files at all.
- `init` is unchanged: it never wrote the names, so the entry's code half is dropped.
- Cargo's comments go too, wink's call: noise, with `/target` already the file's first line.
- So does `/.agent-running`, wink's call: the lock is off, and turning it on puts the line back.
- The set's copy of the lock instruction learns of the leak in a cycle of its own, being an
  agent-file change: filed as a Todo.
- zc-ring-x1 carries the same list and an older leftover, `.bashrc` of 2026-08-27, and is told
  after Land.
- Single-step, a config edit and its notes.

#### Solution

The sandbox's names are ignored nowhere, and the record says why.

- The project's `.gitignore` loses the eleven names, cargo's comments, and the lock's
  `/.agent-running`, keeping the six entries for the build, the scratch, and the repos.
- [session-lock.md](notes/session-lock.md#the-sandboxs-placeholder-files) records what the
  sandbox's placeholder files are, why one session never meets them, what a killed holder leaves
  on disk, and how to find and delete it. Its decision that blamed the `.gitignore` is corrected,
  and the section on turning the lock off names the holder as the kind of command that leaks.
- The set's copy of the lock instruction is a Todo entry, "The set's session-lock file says a
  killed holder leaves files behind".

#### Acceptance check

- An in-sandbox `jj st`, the names unignored, lists only the cycle's edits. Passed.
- wink's own `jj st`, outside the sandbox, lists only the cycle's edits. Passed, run once the
  leftovers were deleted.
- `vc-x1 validate` passes.

#### Ladder

- chore: the sandbox's names leave .gitignore (done)

# References
====
## Todo

Entries are in priority order, the first highest, and reprioritizing is moving an entry. Each is a
`###` heading, so a citation is a link to its anchor. Long-tail entries live in
[todo-backlog.md](notes/todo-backlog.md). Use the [Prose form](agent-data/prose.md#prose-form).
Deeper detail goes in a `notes/` design file (link via `[N]` ref).

### Every repo ignores Claude Code's settings.local.json

(wink + agent, 2026-10-14) Claude Code writes `.claude/settings.local.json` in the project
directory, the per-machine file: `/sandbox` writes it there on its first toggle, and we think a
permission prompt's "don't ask again" adds to it. Its content belongs to one machine and one
history, the sandbox's on or off among it, so it is never committed. iiac-perf's agent-repo is
`.claude`, and there the file is tracked and pushed. The shared `settings.json` beside it stays
visible. One line in each repo covers every layout, nested, external, or single:

- Work-repo, and a single-repo workspace: `/.claude/settings.local.json`. `init` writes neither
  today (`render_work_gitignore` and `GITIGNORE_APP_ONLY` in `src/init.rs`), and vc-x1's own
  `.gitignore` drops its whole-directory `/.claude` for it, so anything else Claude Code writes
  there shows in `jj st` and is reviewed.
- Agent-repo: `/settings.local.json`, which matters only when the agent dir is `.claude`, and
  harms nothing otherwise. `init` writes it into `GITIGNORE_SESSION`, and vc-x1's
  `.agent-session/.gitignore` takes it.
- Decide at the opening: whether `.cc-writes/`, the empty mode-700 directory the sandbox's first
  command makes beside it, gets the same pair (`/.claude/.cc-writes/`, `/.cc-writes/`).
- Record the findings in [session-lock.md](notes/session-lock.md#the-sandboxs-placeholder-files):
  `.claude/` is made on demand, not at launch, `.cc-writes/` by the sandbox's first Bash
  command and `settings.local.json` by `/sandbox`, both tested 2026-10-14 in fresh empty
  directories.
- Later, not this cycle: a warning, at acquaint or in `validate`, when the file exists.
- Not this cycle: a repo that already tracks the file also needs `jj file untrack`. For iiac-perf
  that is a message to its agent.

### The set's session-lock file says a killed holder leaves files behind

(wink + agent, 2026-10-14) [agent-data/session-lock.md](agent-data/session-lock.md#what-is-known)
says the session's background commands end when the session does, and so the lock is never
stale. What it does not say: a holder ended that way skips the sandbox's cleanup, and leaves an
empty read-only file on disk for every path the sandbox protects, `.git/config.lock` among them
([session-lock.md](notes/session-lock.md#the-sandboxs-placeholder-files)). An adopter turning the
lock on should know. An `agent-files` proposal cycle, being a change to the set.

### push --amend folds a stage into the pushed work commit

(wink + agent, 2026-10-11) A later stage of a cycle, its closing most often, adds to the work
commit already pushed, and `vc-x1 push` can only make a new commit on each side. So the one
work-repo commit needs to reference several agent-repo commits. Today that is done by hand:
a `jj squash`, a `jj describe` with a trailer written by hand, and then the push.

- The work-repo side: `push --amend` squashes the working copy into the target commit, the top
  commit of the bookmark, where a plain push would make a new commit of it.
  - The target keeps its change id and gets a new commit id, so the bookmark is rewritten and
    pushed.

`.claude`, and there the file is tracked and pushed. The shared `settings.json` beside it stays
visible. One line in each repo covers every layout, nested, external, or single:

- Work-repo, and a single-repo workspace: `/.claude/settings.local.json`. `init` writes neither
  today (`render_work_gitignore` and `GITIGNORE_APP_ONLY` in `src/init.rs`), and vc-x1's own
  `.gitignore` drops its whole-directory `/.claude` for it, so anything else Claude Code writes
  there shows in `jj st` and is reviewed.
- Agent-repo: `/settings.local.json`, which matters only when the agent dir is `.claude`, and
  harms nothing otherwise. `init` writes it into `GITIGNORE_SESSION`, and vc-x1's
  `.agent-session/.gitignore` takes it.
- Decide at the opening: whether `.cc-writes/`, the empty mode-700 directory the sandbox's first
  command makes beside it, gets the same pair (`/.claude/.cc-writes/`, `/.cc-writes/`).
- Record the findings in [session-lock.md](notes/session-lock.md#the-sandboxs-placeholder-files):
  `.claude/` is made on demand, not at launch, `.cc-writes/` by the sandbox's first Bash
  command and `settings.local.json` by `/sandbox`, both tested 2026-10-14 in fresh empty
  directories.
- Later, not this cycle: a warning, at acquaint or in `validate`, when the file exists.
- Not this cycle: a repo that already tracks the file also needs `jj file untrack`. For iiac-perf
  that is a message to its agent.

### The set's session-lock file says a killed holder leaves files behind

(wink + agent, 2026-10-14) [agent-data/session-lock.md](agent-data/session-lock.md#what-is-known)
says the session's background commands end when the session does, and so the lock is never
stale. What it does not say: a holder ended that way skips the sandbox's cleanup, and leaves an
empty read-only file on disk for every path the sandbox protects, `.git/config.lock` among them
([session-lock.md](notes/session-lock.md#the-sandboxs-placeholder-files)). An adopter turning the
lock on should know. An `agent-files` proposal cycle, being a change to the set.

### push --amend folds a stage into the pushed work commit

(wink + agent, 2026-10-11) A later stage of a cycle, its closing most often, adds to the work
commit already pushed, and `vc-x1 push` can only make a new commit on each side. So the one
work-repo commit needs to reference several agent-repo commits. Today that is done by hand:
a `jj squash`, a `jj describe` with a trailer written by hand, and then the push.

- The work-repo side: `push --amend` squashes the working copy into the target commit, the top
  commit of the bookmark, where a plain push would make a new commit of it.
  - The target keeps its change id and gets a new commit id, so the bookmark is rewritten and
    pushed.

## The In Progress block

A cycle's record, `TODO.md > ## In Progress`, written at the opening
([Opening](../AGENTS.md#opening)), finalized and moved to `## Closed` by the closing commit, and
deleted by the next opening ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)). The picked-up `## Todo`
item is moved here (never copied) and becomes the cycle-record's **provisional items**, all
required, all revised as rungs land. The title is a heading one level below `## In Progress` and the
other five are headings one level below the title (a plain cycle: `###` title, `####` items, and
under a program heading, each one deeper):

- **title**, the cycle's name, what `git log --grep` finds it by
- **problem statement**: what is wrong, a sentence or two
- **solution statement**: what will be done about it, broad. Provisional, and the close-out's commit
  body carries the final one
- **acceptance check**: the measure of "are you finished?", specific enough that a reader can run
  it. Not the per-commit validation, which asks whether the artifact still works. A changed check is
  one of the things the deliberation exists to justify
- **deliberation**: how the other five were decided, one bullet per decision. The bullet's lead
  names the decision and its sentence states it, and the sub-bullets carry the reasons, the
  alternatives weighed, and the costs accepted, so a reader can skim the decisions and read the
  reasons only where they doubt one. `_None._` when there was nothing to deliberate, which is a real
  answer
- **ladder**: one rung per step, `- [<title>][M]` plus `(current)` / `(done)`, with `[M]: #<slug>`
  in the file's `# References`. The markers stay when the block moves to `## Closed`. `<title>` is
  the rung's commit title, `<type>: <desc>` per
  [Conventional-commit shape](prose.md#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--commit), so a moved
  `## Todo` entry is retitled. The closing rung, `<cycle title> closing`, is linked like the rest

The ladder heads the **rung subsections**, one per rung under it, the closing included, headed by
the rung's exact title, so the ladder is their index. Each opens at laddering with an abstract-sized
intent statement (the rung's problem and solution in a sentence or two) and completes at the rung's
landing with the conceptual delta: design points, consequences, deferrals, never a restatement of
the landed commit body. The closing rung's opens with the stub "Closing out the cycle." and
completes at close-out with what closing taught, in problem/solution form, or `_None._`.

A rung is `- [<title>][M] (marker)` and carries no detail beyond that: the title links to the rung's
subsection. A step is identified by its title (prose.md's [Steps are named, not
numbered](prose.md#steps-are-named-not-numbered)), so a title carries no number, no version, and no
SHA. The version-of-record still bumps for every rung and its suffix still encodes the stage, but
that encoding belongs to the manifest and appears nowhere in prose.

A single-step cycle's ladder is one unlinked rung, `- <cycle title> (marker)`, with no subsection
under it: a subsection headed by the title would collide with the title heading's anchor ([Cycle
shape](../AGENTS.md#cycle-shape)).

The block is the cycle's only record. A design finding that must outlive the cycle goes into a
`notes/` file by the rung that made it ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)).

#### Problem

Config parsing lives inside the CLI entry point, so every subcommand that wants a setting reaches
through `main` for it, and a test cannot load a config without building the CLI.

#### Solution

Move config loading into its own module with a single `load` entry point that the CLI and the tests
call alike.

#### Acceptance check

`cargo test` passes with a new test that loads a config from a fixture file without touching `main`,
and `vc-x1 config --validate` reports the same findings as before the move.

#### Deliberation

- one work rung, not two: the parser and the loader were going to be split first and moved second,
  but the move is what forces the split, so doing them together is fewer edits
- the acceptance check compares `config --validate` output rather than asserting on internals, so a
  later rename inside the module does not invalidate it

- [refactor: extract config loader opening][1] (done)
- [refactor: split loader from parser][2] (current)
- [refactor: extract config loader closing][3]

Todo entry into this block, and bump the version-of-record.

##### refactor: split loader from parser

Loading and parsing are one function, so the CLI cannot load without parsing and a test cannot parse
without a file on disk.

* The two jobs share one function and one error type.
  - `config/loader.rs` finds and reads the file, returning the text and its path, so a caller that
    only wants to know which file was read stops here.
  - `config/parser.rs` takes text and returns the schema, so a test hands it a string and never
    touches the filesystem.
    - the error type stays shared for now, since splitting it would change the messages
      `config --validate` prints and the acceptance check compares them
* `main` still reaches into the parse result by field.
  - `main` calls `config::load` and receives the schema, so the field access moves behind the module
    boundary and the CLI no longer knows the file's shape.

##### refactor: extract config loader closing

Closing out the cycle.

content.content:
### Commit-body form

The specimen is [commit-model.md](commit-model.md). A commit body is the [Problem-first
shape](#problem-first-shape) with one addition: a body whose
problem has several sub-problems arranges them by a fixed recursion, so a reader knows what any
bullet is from its marker and its depth. The earlier statement, "a problem statement then a solution
statement, both broad", left that arrangement to taste, and taste converged slowly and separately.

- **An intro paragraph states the general problem**, and defines any word the title assumes. It is
  mandatory. [Prose form](#prose-form) wants it regardless, and a body opening on a bullet is a body
  a `--body` flag can mistake for an option. The problem is *this commit's*, never the cycle's: the
  cycle's problem lives in the In Progress block, and a body whose problems outnumber what the diff
  resolves is describing something larger than the commit.
- **`*` bullets are the problem's facets**: sub-problems that decompose the intro's general problem,
  not a grab-bag of unrelated fixes. A body reaching for unrelated problem bullets is usually asking
  to be more than one commit.
- **`-` bullets are solutions**, and every `-` sits under a `*`, solving that facet. A `-` with no
  `*` above it reads as a solution to nothing, so there are no top-level solutions: a solution that
  retires every facet at once is written under each, or the facets are one.
- **One facet is the trivial commit**: the intro, one `*`, one or more `-` under it. Not a second
  form, the general form at its smallest.
- **A bookend body is a pointer**: an opening or closing commit resolves no problem of its own, so
  its body is the intro paragraph alone, naming the cycle by its title and pointing at its record,
  the In Progress block. No `*`, no `-`.

**The markers are typed on purpose**: `*` always means problem, `-` always means solution, and the
pairing is what a reader counts on: the `-` answers the `*` above it, with no rule to consult. The
typing also keeps history greppable (`^\* ` finds every facet, `^ - ` every solution). Bodies are
read as plain text, in `jj log` and in terminals, where the markers survive, and if a renderer ever
flattens them the indentation still carries the structure. So the mixed markers are deliberate, and
a linter's consistent-marker rule is wrong to normalize them.

Unchanged by this: no version in title or body, no file list, no deliberation, titles per
[Conventional-commit shape](#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--commit).

### Conventional-commit shape (ladder / commit)

([why](rationale.md#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--commit))

A ladder step and its commit description share a *title* shape, a [Conventional
Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/) title (`<type>: <desc>`, an optional
`(scope)` after the type: `feat(push): ...`) over [Prose form](#prose-form) detail. They differ in
the title's marker (below) and in bullet *content*: commit bodies take the [Commit-body
form](#commit-body-form), the ladder's are conceptual (see "Bullet *content* differs by surface"
above). The shared template:

```
<title>                          # <title> is the commit's `<type>: <desc>`
<optional prose intro>
  - <optional item>
    <optional prose intro>
      - <optional sub-item>
      ...
```

The two surfaces apply it as:

- **Ladder step** (`TODO.md` `## In Progress`): the rung is `- [<title>][M] (marker)`: the title
  reference-linked to the rung's subsection via `[M]: #<slug>` in the file's `# References` (the
  closing rung linked like the rest), and the `(current)` / `(done)` marker. Its position in the
  list is its position in the ladder. The last rung is the close-out and its text says so. Detail
  lives not on the rung but in its subsection under the ladder, headed by the rung's exact
  title (see the protocol's [Opening](../AGENTS.md#opening)), bulleted, never `;`-joined inline.
- **Commit description**: no prefix. The title is the first line, and the body is the prose (see
  [Commit description](../AGENTS.md#commit-description)).

The title is **identical** across both for a given step, so a step's ladder entry and its commit
title line up verbatim. The rung's subsection heading carries the same title, a third
surface on every rung (the closing rung's exists only when close-out gotchas occurred: see the
protocol's [Opening](../AGENTS.md#opening)). Pick the commit title first and reuse it.

That identity is **per step**, not per cycle: each step in a cycle gets its own distinct descriptive
title, never one shared cycle title uniquified by a step marker. The block's title heading carries
the *cycle title*, the bare name no multi-step commit carries (see the bookends below). To keep a
cycle's commits collectable with one `git log --grep`, give the step titles a common greppable stem
(e.g. `config loader`).

**Cycle bookend titles**: a multi-step cycle's bookend commits are the cycle title plus a suffix, "
opening" and " closing", same type (`feat: dynamic warmup opening` /
`feat: dynamic warmup closing`), so one `git log --grep "<cycle title>"` returns the pair that
brackets the ladder. The bare cycle title is the cycle's *name*: the block's title heading carries
it, and no multi-step commit does, which is also what keeps the closing rung's subsection anchor
clear of the title heading's. A single-step cycle's one commit is the cycle and keeps the bare
title, in both repos and in its one ladder rung ([Cycle shape](../AGENTS.md#cycle-shape)). The type
repeats across the pair even though the bookends are mostly bookkeeping: identical prefixes make
them scannable. Rungs between keep their own titles on the stem.

### Commit titles and descriptions

([why](rationale.md#commit-titles-and-descriptions))

The vocabulary over the structure: [Conventional-commit
shape](#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--commit) holds what a title and body are shaped like, and
this section holds what may fill them. The title is a [Conventional
Commit](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/), `<type>: <short description>` with an optional
`(scope)`, at the width in [Line widths](#line-widths). The body is the [Commit-body
form](#commit-body-form), wrapped per Line widths, with no version in title or body, no file list,
and no deliberation. `vc-x1 push` gives both repos' commits the same title and body. `ochid:` is
the body's last line, stamped by push, and a breaking change uses the hyphenated
`BREAKING-CHANGE:` trailer key.

#### Conventional commit types

The common types: `feat`, `fix`, `refactor`, `test`, `docs`, `chore`. A type beyond the common set
is a declared one ([Project-declared types](#project-declared-types)), and a title check admits
exactly the two vocabularies.

#### Conventional commit scopes

A scope names a component as its user would name it (a subcommand, a repo), never a file or
directory, and is omitted when there is none. A declared type's scope slot carries its
declaration's vocabulary instead ([Project-declared types](#project-declared-types)).

#### Project-declared types

Beyond the common types, a project may declare its own when a recurring kind of work deserves one
searchable token. The declaration names the type, its scope vocabulary, and its description
grammar, so a reader can parse the titles and a title check can admit them by name, and the scope

### Commit-body form

The specimen is [commit-model.md](commit-model.md). A commit body is the [Problem-first
shape](#problem-first-shape) with one addition: a body whose
problem has several sub-problems arranges them by a fixed recursion, so a reader knows what any
bullet is from its marker and its depth. The earlier statement, "a problem statement then a solution
statement, both broad", left that arrangement to taste, and taste converged slowly and separately.

- **An intro paragraph states the general problem**, and defines any word the title assumes. It is
  mandatory. [Prose form](#prose-form) wants it regardless, and a body opening on a bullet is a body
  a `--body` flag can mistake for an option. The problem is *this commit's*, never the cycle's: the
  cycle's problem lives in the In Progress block, and a body whose problems outnumber what the diff
  resolves is describing something larger than the commit.
- **`*` bullets are the problem's facets**: sub-problems that decompose the intro's general problem,
  not a grab-bag of unrelated fixes. A body reaching for unrelated problem bullets is usually asking
  to be more than one commit.
- **`-` bullets are solutions**, and every `-` sits under a `*`, solving that facet. A `-` with no
  `*` above it reads as a solution to nothing, so there are no top-level solutions: a solution that
  retires every facet at once is written under each, or the facets are one.
- **One facet is the trivial commit**: the intro, one `*`, one or more `-` under it. Not a second
  form, the general form at its smallest.
- **A bookend body is a pointer**: an opening or closing commit resolves no problem of its own, so
  its body is the intro paragraph alone, naming the cycle by its title and pointing at its record,
  the In Progress block. No `*`, no `-`.

**The markers are typed on purpose**: `*` always means problem, `-` always means solution, and the
pairing is what a reader counts on: the `-` answers the `*` above it, with no rule to consult. The
typing also keeps history greppable (`^\* ` finds every facet, `^ - ` every solution). Bodies are
read as plain text, in `jj log` and in terminals, where the markers survive, and if a renderer ever
flattens them the indentation still carries the structure. So the mixed markers are deliberate, and
a linter's consistent-marker rule is wrong to normalize them.

Unchanged by this: no version in title or body, no file list, no deliberation, titles per
[Conventional-commit shape](#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--commit).

### Conventional-commit shape (ladder / commit)

([why](rationale.md#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--commit))

A ladder step and its commit description share a *title* shape, a [Conventional
Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/) title (`<type>: <desc>`, an optional
`(scope)` after the type: `feat(push): ...`) over [Prose form](#prose-form) detail. They differ in
the title's marker (below) and in bullet *content*: commit bodies take the [Commit-body
form](#commit-body-form), the ladder's are conceptual (see "Bullet *content* differs by surface"
above). The shared template:

```
<title>                          # <title> is the commit's `<type>: <desc>`
<optional prose intro>
  - <optional item>
    <optional prose intro>
      - <optional sub-item>
      ...
```

The two surfaces apply it as:

- **Ladder step** (`TODO.md` `## In Progress`): the rung is `- [<title>][M] (marker)`: the title
  reference-linked to the rung's subsection via `[M]: #<slug>` in the file's `# References` (the
  closing rung linked like the rest), and the `(current)` / `(done)` marker. Its position in the
  list is its position in the ladder. The last rung is the close-out and its text says so. Detail
  lives not on the rung but in its subsection under the ladder, headed by the rung's exact
  title (see the protocol's [Opening](../AGENTS.md#opening)), bulleted, never `;`-joined inline.
- **Commit description**: no prefix. The title is the first line, and the body is the prose (see
  [Commit description](../AGENTS.md#commit-description)).

[package]
name = "vc-x1"
version = "0.84.32"
edition = "2024"

# Single-name convention (chores-16, 0.78.3): the package name IS
# the installed binary's name, `vc-x1` on main and a per-line dev
# name on a branch (renamed at cycle open, back at close-out, next
# to the version bump). The guard against a forgotten open-rename
# is build.rs, which refuses to build a suffixed version under the
# stable name on every cargo verb, `cargo install` included.

//! Export the resolved `jj-lib` version as `JJ_LIB_VERSION`,
//! guard the single-name convention, and generate the config
//! schema from the `vc-config.md` prototype.
//!
//! jj-lib exports no version constant of its own, so the only
//! statement of what this binary links against is the resolved
//! version in `Cargo.lock`:
//!
//! - the lock is read from `$CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` directly, not by
//!   walking ancestors: we are not a workspace, and a walk can
//!   bind a sibling project's lock, which is worse than failing.
//! - a missing or jj-lib-less lock fails the build rather than
//!   emitting an "unknown" that would later be reported as fact.
//!
//! The name guard (chores-16, 0.78.3): a suffixed version marks a
//! dev rung, and a dev rung must never carry the stable package
//! name, or installing it replaces the stable `vc-x1` binary with
//! unpushed code. It lives here rather than in a `#[test]` because
//! `cargo install` never runs tests: a build script runs on every
//! cargo verb, so the forbidden combination fails to compile at
//! all, install included.

use std::path::Path;

// The md -> toml filter, the same file the binary compiles as
// `crate::md_fence`: the prototype and a `.vc-config.md` are one
// format, so they are read by one implementation. A build script
// is its own crate, so it reaches the file by `#[path]` rather
// than by a crate-relative module path.
#[path = "src/md_fence.rs"]
mod md_fence;

use md_fence::md_to_toml;

/// Extract `jj-lib`'s resolved version from `Cargo.lock` text.
///
/// Scans for the `[[package]]` block whose `name` is `jj-lib` and
/// returns that block's `version`. Line-based rather than a TOML
/// parse: build scripts get no dev-dependencies, and the lock's
/// shape is fixed by cargo.

## The sandbox's placeholder files

What the empty files are, found 2026-10-14 in the cycle `chore: the sandbox's names leave
.gitignore`. The sandbox protects a list of paths for the life of each command it runs: the
dotfiles at the workspace root, a dozen names under `.claude`, and `.git/config.lock` among them.

- A protected path that exists is mounted read-only over itself. One that does not exist gets an
  empty file made on disk to mount over, with `/dev/null` mounted on it, and the file is removed
  when the command ends.
- Seen directly in the sandbox's arguments, 2026-10-14. The sandbox is `bwrap`, which `claude`
  starts in place of the shell, and it carries a `--ro-bind /dev/null <path>` for each protected
  path that does not exist: 23 in this workspace, `.bashrc`, `.git/config.lock`, and
  `.claude/skills` among them. `bwrap` makes every mount before it starts the bash that runs the
  command, so no shell or program inside the command bears on the files.
- Inside the command the missing paths read as character devices, and jj snapshots no device. An
  in-sandbox `jj st` with none of the names ignored listed nothing of them.
- Outside the command the empty files are on disk while it runs, and only then. That is what the
  second session's snapshot caught in [What two sessions do with no
  lock](#what-two-sessions-do-with-no-lock), and what wink's editor showed on 2026-10-14: the
  names in Zed's list of changes for some seconds while an agent command ran, gone when it ended.
- Tested the same day, wink watching Zed: an agent command that wrote a file under `tmp/` and
  slept 20 seconds showed the eleven root names for those seconds and no longer. The same work done
  by Python showed them the same. The same command with the sandbox turned off showed none, the
  same shell starting it, so it is the sandbox around a command and not the shell or the program.
- So the agent alone never commits them. A snapshot taken from outside while an agent command
  runs records them, and the agent's next snapshot drops them again. A commit made from outside
  in that window keeps them.
- So no `.gitignore` names them, in a project or a user's global one. An ignored name hides a
  file a user makes there: it is never committed, and nothing says so until a clone comes up
  without it. The list is also Claude Code's and changes with a release, and some of its names,
  `.vscode` or `.mcp.json`, are files a project may track.
- A command that is killed rather than ended keeps them. The lock's holder, started at
  2026-10-11T21:09:22Z under the lock's tests, left 24 files in this workspace, every one empty,
  mode 0444, and born that second: eleven at the root, twelve under `.claude`, and
  `.git/config.lock`. The tests ended sessions by Ctrl+C, `kill -9`, the close button, and
  unplugging, and we think one of them killed the holder before its cleanup ran.
  - Left on disk they are real files, which every snapshot sees, in the sandbox or out.
    `.git/config.lock` fails every `git config` write, and an empty `.claude/skills` keeps the
    directory from being made.
  - Nobody saw them for three days: the eleven at the root were in the hand-written ignore of
    2026-08-27, and the rest are under `.claude` or `.git`. The ignore came out, and they showed.
  - Found from outside a session by `find . -type f -size 0 -perm 0444`, and deleted from there.
    Inside a session they are read-only mounts and cannot be.
- Not tested: whether a background command that ends by itself removes its files.

## Turned off

**`--use-template`**. Value is `CODE[,BOT]`. If `BOT` is omitted, defaults to the sibling directory
`<CODE>.claude` (file-name concat, not path join, since the two templates are not nested).
Non-hidden contents are copied recursively into each target, and hidden entries (names starting with
`.`) are skipped since init creates the repo's own hidden files (`.vc-config.md`, `.gitignore`,
`.git/`, `.jj/`). If either template has a `README.md` at its root, its first line is rewritten to
`# <repo-name>`: `<name>` for the work repo and `<name>.claude` for the bot repo. For local
verification without hitting GitHub, combine `--use-template` with `--repo local=<PARENT>`.

**`--adopt`**. Without it an existing TARGET is refused, named by what it holds. With it, init
grows the target into a dual workspace:

- A plain directory, no repo: both repos are created around it, and everything in it that its
  `.gitignore` does not exclude is the work repo's first commit, whatever the file sizes. Files
  over jj's new-file size limit (1MiB by default) are listed, since jj would otherwise leave them
  out. A `.gitignore` it already has is kept and given the agent directory's line.
- A jj repo colocated with git and with no workspace config: its history stays, and one commit,
  "Adopt as a dual-repo workspace", goes on top, carrying `.vc-config.md`, the `.gitignore` line,
  and the `ochid:` trailer to the agent repo's first commit. With an `origin`, the agent repo's
  remote is derived beside it, `--repo` and `--account` are refused, and the work side pushes
  nothing: the commit is yours to land. With no origin, the remotes come from `--repo` as for a
...

Always test against a throwaway fixture, never the live workspace. Scaffold one with `vc-x1 init
<TARGET> --repo local=<PARENT>` (no GitHub, no network), then run the complete flow end-to-end. The
work repo uses plain `jj git push`, and the bot repo uses `vc-x1 squash-push` to squash trailing
writes and push in one shot.

`--repo local=<PARENT>` lays out:
```
<PARENT>/
  remote-work.git/     bare git remote for the work repo
  remote-bot.git/   bare git remote for the .claude bot repo
  <NAME>/              work repo (jj colocated, main tracks origin)
    .vc-config.md      work=".", agent=".claude"
    .gitignore         /.claude /.git /.jj /target
    .claude/           bot repo (jj colocated, main tracks origin)
      .vc-config.md    work="..", agent="."
      .gitignore       .git .jj
```

```bash
parent=$(mktemp -u /tmp/vc-x1-test-XXXXXX)
vc-x1 init "$parent/work" --repo local="$parent"
work="$parent/work"
bot="$parent/work/.claude"

# 1. work repo: described commit -> advance main -> push
...
The decisions behind it:

- A repo is a `.git` or a `.jj` in the target itself. Adopt takes a jj repo colocated with git and
  points a git-only one at `jj git init --colocate`. A working copy with uncommitted work is
  refused, since adopt's commit would take it in.
- An adopted repo's commit, "Adopt as a dual-repo workspace", carries `.vc-config.md`, the
  `.gitignore` line, and the `ochid:` trailer, and goes on top of its history. With an `origin`,
  the work side pushes nothing, that commit being the user's to land, and the agent repo's remote
  is derived beside the origin, the provisioner read off its URL. With no origin, the remotes come
  from `--repo` as a fresh init's do.
- The `--repo` chain needs the user config, which a repo with an origin does not, so under
  `--adopt` the chain's error is held and raised only when the target has no origin.
- A single-repo workspace's config is edited by adding lines only, `agent =` after the last key of
  `[repos]` and `agent-repo =` under `[remote]`, with prose, comments, and other keys untouched.
  The file is read back and restored when it does not declare both keys.
- An adopted directory's `.gitignore` is kept and given the agent directory's line.
- The first commit tracks every file whatever its size, since jj leaves a new file over
  `snapshot.max-new-file-size` untracked, and names the ones over the limit.
- `--use-template` is refused with `--adopt`, since a template would overwrite files of the same
  name.

## Markdown anchor links

GitHub anchor algorithm: lowercase, strip non-alphanumeric characters in place, map remaining spaces
to hyphens 1-for-1. Do **not** collapse adjacent whitespace, so `a + b` -> `a--b` (spaces on both
sides of `+`), but `a: b` -> `a-b` (only trailing space on `:`). General markdown reference:
[markdownguide.org](https://www.markdownguide.org). GitHub publishes no official spec for
auto-generated anchors. The de-facto reference implementation is
[github-slugger](https://github.com/Flet/github-slugger).

## In Progress

### feat: every repo ignores Claude Code's settings.local.json

(wink + agent, 2026-10-14, picked 2026-10-15) Claude Code writes `.claude/settings.local.json` in
the project directory, the per-machine file: `/sandbox` writes it there on its first toggle, and
we think a permission prompt's "don't ask again" adds to it. Its content belongs to one machine
and one history, the sandbox's on or off among it, so it is never committed. iiac-perf's
agent-repo is `.claude`, and there the file is tracked and pushed. The shared `settings.json`
beside it stays visible. One line in each repo covers every layout, nested, external, or single:

- Work-repo, and a single-repo workspace: `/.claude/settings.local.json`. `init` writes neither
  today (`render_work_gitignore` and `GITIGNORE_APP_ONLY` in `src/init.rs`), and vc-x1's own
  `.gitignore` drops its whole-directory `/.claude` for it, so anything else Claude Code writes
  there shows in `jj st` and is reviewed.
- Agent-repo: `/settings.local.json`, which matters only when the agent dir is `.claude`, and
  harms nothing otherwise. `init` writes it into `GITIGNORE_SESSION`, and vc-x1's
  `.agent-session/.gitignore` takes it.
- Decide at the opening: whether `.cc-writes/`, the empty mode-700 directory the sandbox's first
  command makes beside it, gets the same pair (`/.claude/.cc-writes/`, `/.cc-writes/`).
- Record the findings in [session-lock.md](notes/session-lock.md#the-sandboxs-placeholder-files):
  `.claude/` is made on demand, not at launch, `.cc-writes/` by the sandbox's first Bash
  command and `settings.local.json` by `/sandbox`, both tested 2026-10-14 in fresh empty
  directories.
- Later, not this cycle: a warning, at acquaint or in `validate`, when the file exists.
- Not this cycle: a repo that already tracks the file also needs `jj file untrack`. For iiac-perf
  that is a message to its agent.

#### Deliberation

- The rules bend by wink's waiver of 2026-10-15: "permission granted to complete the change and
  commits and ready it for landing on main".
  - It covers the work review, the description review, and the approval of each push, the
    bookmark's included, through the close-out.
  - Land is not inside it, and waits for wink's go.
- The cycle carries `next-time`'s commit, which held the Todo entry and the continuation note,
  wink's call: the bookmark is renamed to this cycle's, and the commit stays under it.
  - The commit was published, and its pair on the agent-repo's `main` carries a trailer naming
    it. Carrying it keeps the pair, where redoing its two edits here would leave that trailer
    naming an abandoned commit.
  - The cost accepted: the bookmark holds two commits, and the fast-forward at Land takes both.
- Single-step: config lines, the `init` renderers with their tests, and the notes, one solution.
- `.cc-writes/` is ignored nowhere: jj and git record files, never directories, and it holds none.
  Should Claude Code ever write a file into it, the file shows in `jj st` and is reviewed, which
  is why the work-repo's ignore narrows to one file.
- The agent-repo's tracked `settings.local.json` is deleted, wink's call. Claude Code reads
  project settings from the project's `.claude/` only, and the agent dir left that name on
  2026-09-28. The file's last change was 2026-08-28, its rules name `.claude` as the agent-repo,
  and no code or agent-file reads it.
- `.agent-session/.claude/`, an empty `.cc-writes/` of 2026-10-09 and nothing else, was deleted
  at acquaint, wink's go. Untracked, so no commit carries it.
- The second continuation note was stale at acquaint: `.claude/` is writable again and its
  `settings.local.json` turns the sandbox on, so its restore steps are moot. Reset with the first.

#### Solution

The project's own repos and every workspace `init` makes ignore `settings.local.json` by one line
each, and the work-repo stops ignoring the rest of `.claude/`. Provisional.

#### Acceptance check

- The work-repo's `jj st` does not list `.claude/settings.local.json`, the file on disk, and the
  commit's tree has no path under `.claude/`.
- The agent-repo's commit has no `settings.local.json`, and its `.gitignore` names it.
- A fresh `init` in `tmp/`, dual and single-repo, writes the lines, checked by the `init` tests
  and by reading the files.
- `vc-x1 validate` passes.

#### Ladder

- feat: every repo ignores Claude Code's settings.local.json (current)

## In Progress

### feat: every repo ignores Claude Code's settings.local.json

(wink + agent, 2026-10-14, picked 2026-10-15) Claude Code writes `.claude/settings.local.json` in
the project directory, the per-machine file: `/sandbox` writes it there on its first toggle, and
we think a permission prompt's "don't ask again" adds to it. Its content belongs to one machine
and one history, the sandbox's on or off among it, so it is never committed. iiac-perf's
agent-repo is `.claude`, and there the file is tracked and pushed. The shared `settings.json`
beside it stays visible. One line in each repo covers every layout, nested, external, or single:

- Work-repo, and a single-repo workspace: `/.claude/settings.local.json`. `init` writes neither
  today (`render_work_gitignore` and `GITIGNORE_APP_ONLY` in `src/init.rs`), and vc-x1's own
  `.gitignore` drops its whole-directory `/.claude` for it, so anything else Claude Code writes
  there shows in `jj st` and is reviewed.
- Agent-repo: `/settings.local.json`, which matters only when the agent dir is `.claude`, and
  harms nothing otherwise. `init` writes it into `GITIGNORE_SESSION`, and vc-x1's
  `.agent-session/.gitignore` takes it.
- Decide at the opening: whether `.cc-writes/`, the empty mode-700 directory the sandbox's first
  command makes beside it, gets the same pair (`/.claude/.cc-writes/`, `/.cc-writes/`).
- Record the findings in [session-lock.md](notes/session-lock.md#the-sandboxs-placeholder-files):
  `.claude/` is made on demand, not at launch, `.cc-writes/` by the sandbox's first Bash
  command and `settings.local.json` by `/sandbox`, both tested 2026-10-14 in fresh empty
  directories.
- Later, not this cycle: a warning, at acquaint or in `validate`, when the file exists.
- Not this cycle: a repo that already tracks the file also needs `jj file untrack`. For iiac-perf
  that is a message to its agent.

#### Deliberation

- The rules bend by wink's waiver of 2026-10-15: "permission granted to complete the change and
  commits and ready it for landing on main".
  - It covers the work review, the description review, and the approval of each push, the
    bookmark's included, through the close-out.
  - Land is not inside it, and waits for wink's go.
- The cycle carries `next-time`'s commit, which held the Todo entry and the continuation note,
  wink's call: the bookmark is renamed to this cycle's, and the commit stays under it.
  - The commit was published, and its pair on the agent-repo's `main` carries a trailer naming
    it. Carrying it keeps the pair, where redoing its two edits here would leave that trailer
    naming an abandoned commit.
  - The cost accepted: the bookmark holds two commits, and the fast-forward at Land takes both.
- Single-step: config lines, the `init` renderers with their tests, and the notes, one solution.
- `.cc-writes/` is ignored nowhere: jj and git record files, never directories, and it holds none.
  Should Claude Code ever write a file into it, the file shows in `jj st` and is reviewed, which
  is why the work-repo's ignore narrows to one file.
- The agent-repo's tracked `settings.local.json` is deleted, wink's call. Claude Code reads
  project settings from the project's `.claude/` only, and the agent dir left that name on
  2026-09-28. The file's last change was 2026-08-28, its rules name `.claude` as the agent-repo,
  and no code or agent-file reads it.
- `.agent-session/.claude/`, an empty `.cc-writes/` of 2026-10-09 and nothing else, was deleted
  at acquaint, wink's go. Untracked, so no commit carries it.
- The second continuation note was stale at acquaint: `.claude/` is writable again and its
  `settings.local.json` turns the sandbox on, so its restore steps are moot. Reset with the first.

#### Solution

The project's own repos and every workspace `init` makes ignore `settings.local.json` by one line
each, and the work-repo stops ignoring the rest of `.claude/`. Provisional.

#### Acceptance check

- The work-repo's `jj st` does not list `.claude/settings.local.json`, the file on disk, and the
  commit's tree has no path under `.claude/`.
- The agent-repo's commit has no `settings.local.json`, and its `.gitignore` names it.
- A fresh `init` in `tmp/`, dual and single-repo, writes the lines, checked by the `init` tests
  and by reading the files.
- `vc-x1 validate` passes.

#### Ladder

# Todo Backlog

Lower-priority `## Todo` entries, the long tail. When an entry becomes a priority, move it (and
any refs it cites) into `TODO.md > ## Todo` at its place in the order.

Same shape as `TODO.md > ## Todo`, [Todo format](../agent-data/notes.md#todo-format).

## Todo

### vc-x1 takes a lock of its own for a run that writes

(wink + agent, 2026-10-11) Two `vc-x1` runs in one workspace can overlap, a user's two terminals
included, and nothing serializes them. A lock for it was considered and is not added, wink's call,
2026-10-13: what it costs is more than what it prevents here, the reason the session lock was
turned off ([session-lock.md](session-lock.md#turned-off)). The design is kept for the day the
overlap is met in real use.

- What would reopen it: two runs overlapping outside a test. The one overlap seen was made on
  purpose, two pushes started in the same second in the tests of 2026-10-12. One died with
  `error: Concurrent checkout` partway, and the other took the first's agent-repo commit as its
  partner, so two work commits name one ([What two sessions do with no
  lock](session-lock.md#what-two-sessions-do-with-no-lock)).
- What jj covers: two jj commands run at once do not corrupt a repo. We think each records an
  operation and the next command merges the two, from what we know of jj and not from a test.
- What jj does not cover: a sequence. A `vc-x1 push` is a commit in each repo, the trailers that
  pair them, and two pushes to the remotes, and jj serializes each of those and not the run.
- The overlap that is left: a user's run started beside the agent's, two of the user's own, or two
  sessions' runs, the session lock being off. [At
  rest](../AGENTS.md#at-rest-push-stop-squash-push) has the agent stop before the user
  squash-pushes, which keeps the first of them rare.

## In Progress

### feat: every repo ignores Claude Code's settings.local.json

(wink + agent, 2026-10-14, picked 2026-10-15) Claude Code writes `.claude/settings.local.json` in
the project directory, the per-machine file: `/sandbox` writes it there on its first toggle, and
we think a permission prompt's "don't ask again" adds to it. Its content belongs to one machine
and one history, the sandbox's on or off among it, so it is never committed. iiac-perf's
agent-repo is `.claude`, and there the file is tracked and pushed. The shared `settings.json`
beside it stays visible. One line in each repo covers every layout, nested, external, or single:

- Work-repo, and a single-repo workspace: `/.claude/settings.local.json`. `init` writes neither
  today (`render_work_gitignore` and `GITIGNORE_APP_ONLY` in `src/init.rs`), and vc-x1's own

on or off among them, in `.claude/settings.local.json`, its local
project settings, a file never meant to be committed. The work-repo

copy from when it was `.claude`, and the repos `init` makes ignored it
nowhere.

  writes in `.claude/`.

    reviewed, and the file already in the working copy is untracked.

  since the agent dir stopped being `.claude`.

    which matters wherever an agent dir is `.claude`.

    single repo's `.gitignore` and the agent-side line into the
    agent-repo's, and gives an adopted `.gitignore` the line when it
    lacks it.
* The notes said nothing of what `.claude/` holds beyond the
  sandbox's placeholders.

    `settings.local.json` and why only the second is ignored, the

    warning is filed in the backlog.

You're right on both points. Locally the cycle is now a single rung, but I haven't pushed it. Making that true on the remote means rewriting the published bookmark, so I'm stopping for your go.

**On "per-machine":** that word came from the Todo entry, and I carried it everywhere. You're right that the file is project-level. I'd avoid calling it "user level", though. In Claude Code's own terms, "user settings" means `~/.claude/settings.json`, which applies to all of one person's projects. Claude Code calls `.claude/settings.local.json` the **local project settings**: one user's personal settings for one project, never committed.

I've reworded it to "local project settings, one user's for this project" in every place it appeared:
- `src/init.rs` (three doc comments)
- `notes/session-lock.md`, `notes/vc-x1-init.md`, and `notes/todo-backlog.md`
- the record in `zCLOSED.md`
- the commit description's intro

**On the single rung:** I folded `next-time`'s commit into the cycle's commit. There's now one commit directly on `main`, with the same title and its `ochid:` trailer kept by hand. My first fold went wrong: it re-applied `next-time`'s edits that the cycle commit had already undone. I reset the commit's files to their state just before the fold and checked them against that snapshot: no differences. Full validation passes.

I updated the record's deliberation to match. It now says the commit was folded at your call, and that the "per-machine" wording was corrected.

**Two costs of the rewrite you should accept or not:**
- The agent-repo commit paired with `next-time` (`da4850c2`, already on the agent-repo's `main`) has a trailer naming the folded commit, which will no longer exist.
- The agent-repo's copy of the first push's description still says "one machine's settings". That repo's `main` is published, so I can't rewrite it.

Go for the force-push of the bookmark? It would be `jj git push --bookmark feat-every-repo-ignores-claude-codes-settingslocaljson -R .`.

## Trapezoid close-out recipe

The reshape behind the trapezoid shape, run at [Land](#cycle-bookmarks-create-and-land) step 2: the
close-out commit, pushed linearly by the closing rung, becomes a merge whose first parent is the
trunk line and whose second parent is the cycle's ladder. Nothing here publishes, the merge goes out
with Land's fast-forward.

```
  main line   ...--<base>------------------<closeout>--
                      \                    /
  ladder             <rung-1>--...--<tip>-+
```

- `<base>`: the **parent of the ladder's first rung**, the trunk position when the cycle opened. It
  becomes the first parent. Not always the previous close-out: a cycle landed linearly since
  (keep-separate shape, or a single-step cycle) sits on the trunk line and must stay there.
